title: Event Production & Live Operations Core v1

domain.name: Event Production & Live Operations
domain.description: Practical event planning, run-of-show, venues, vendors, staffing, AV, guest flow, safety, contingency, and live execution.

competencies.name: Event Scope, Budget & Objectives
competencies.description: Translate an event concept into goals, audience, scope, budget, constraints, and success criteria.
competencies.purpose: Keep production choices aligned with event purpose.

units.title: Event brief workflow
units.content: Define purpose, audience, date, venue assumptions, guest count, experience priorities, budget ceiling, non-negotiables, approvals, and success measures.

units.title: Every extra moment has a cost
units.content: Program additions affect time, staffing, AV, venue, guest flow, and contingency; scope changes should update the whole plan.

units.title: Scope failures
units.content: Avoid planning from aesthetics alone, hiding contingency needs, accepting unlimited revisions, and budgeting without labor, rentals, transport, or strike time.

drills.title: Build an event brief
drills.prompt: Create a complete brief for a mid-size client event.

competencies.name: Run of Show & Production Timeline
competencies.description: Build minute-by-minute cues, dependencies, responsibilities, and transitions.
competencies.purpose: Turn the event plan into an executable live sequence.

units.title: ROS workflow
units.content: List program beats; add setup and transition time; assign cue owner; mark dependencies; include vendor call times; add decision points and contingency notes; distribute controlled versions.

units.title: Transitions are real time
units.content: A schedule that budgets content but not movement, reset, mic handoff, or room turnover will run late.

units.title: Timeline failures
units.content: Avoid unexplained abbreviations, multiple conflicting versions, impossible turnovers, and cue ownership that exists only in one person's head.

drills.title: Build a run of show
drills.prompt: Create a run of show for an event with speeches, media, meal service, and entertainment.

competencies.name: Venue, Load-In & Guest Flow
competencies.description: Plan access, loading, room layout, entrances, parking, backstage, storage, and strike.

units.title: Venue logistics walk
units.content: Map arrival routes, loading, storage, power, exits, restrooms, guest circulation, staff zones, vendor staging, accessibility, and strike path.

units.title: Separate flows when possible
units.content: Guest, catering, equipment, talent, and waste movement should not compete for the same path at the same time.

units.title: Venue failures
units.content: Avoid blocking exits, relying on unverified loading access, staging cases in guest paths, and assuming venue rules or capacities without confirmation.

drills.title: Design a venue flow plan
drills.prompt: Review a venue layout and identify operational zones and conflict points.

competencies.name: Event Vendor & Crew Coordination
competencies.description: Coordinate caterers, decorators, photo/video, entertainment, rentals, transportation, and venue teams.
competencies.purpose: Align multiple contributors around one operating plan.

units.title: Vendor coordination
units.content: Confirm scope, contacts, arrival, load-in, dependencies, equipment, access, approvals, teardown, and escalation path for each contributor.

units.title: One owner per dependency
units.content: Shared responsibility often means nobody owns the handoff; assign a named production owner for every critical dependency.

units.title: Coordination failures
units.content: Avoid assuming vendors talked to each other, changing instructions in private side conversations, and withholding updated timelines from affected teams.

drills.title: Build a vendor coordination grid
drills.prompt: Create a coordination sheet for a multi-vendor event.

competencies.name: AV, Power & Live Production Safety
competencies.description: Coordinate audio, video, lighting, playback, connectivity, and power with qualified production personnel.
competencies.purpose: Deliver reliable technical production without unsafe electrical or rigging improvisation.

units.title: Technical production has hard safety boundaries
units.content: Temporary power, rigging, overhead loads, high-current distribution, and structural attachment require competent qualified personnel and venue-approved methods.

units.title: AV readiness workflow
units.content: Confirm source formats, playback backups, mic plan, signal paths, cable routes, power requirements, internet needs, rehearsal, and qualified ownership for power or rigging.

units.title: AV safety failures
units.content: Do not overload circuits, defeat grounding, hang overhead equipment without approved rigging, run trip hazards across egress, or improvise structural attachment.

drills.title: Review an AV plan
drills.prompt: Identify reliability and safety gaps in an event AV plan.

competencies.name: Guest Safety, Capacity & Emergency Readiness
competencies.description: Plan staffing, capacities, emergency contacts, weather response, medical escalation, and crowd movement.
competencies.purpose: Support a safe event environment and rapid response.

units.title: Safety planning
units.content: Confirm venue capacity and emergency procedures; identify responsible authority; brief staff on exits, emergency contacts, weather triggers, accessibility needs, and stop-work escalation.

units.title: Venue emergency plan governs onsite response
units.content: Production teams should align with the venue and qualified authorities rather than inventing their own emergency rules.

units.title: Safety failures
units.content: Avoid exceeding confirmed capacity, obstructing egress, ignoring severe weather or medical escalation, and assigning untrained staff to specialized emergency roles.

drills.title: Build a pre-event safety brief
drills.prompt: Create a concise staff safety briefing for a live event.

competencies.name: Show Calling & Live Issue Management
competencies.description: Call cues, track timing, coordinate changes, and manage live problems without cascading confusion.
competencies.purpose: Keep the event coherent when conditions change.

units.title: Live control loop
units.content: Observe current state; communicate one clear decision; update affected cue owners; protect guest safety and critical commitments; record deviations; rebase the timeline.

units.title: Stabilize before optimizing
units.content: During a live failure, restore a safe workable state first; perfect polish comes second.

units.title: Live-management failures
units.content: Avoid multiple people calling conflicting cues, making silent schedule changes, skipping safety checks to recover time, and hiding a material issue from decision owners.

drills.title: Recover from a show delay
drills.prompt: Replan a run of show after a 20-minute production delay.

competencies.name: Event Closeout & Postmortem
competencies.description: Handle strike, rentals, payments, asset return, incident notes, deliverables, and lessons learned.
competencies.purpose: Turn event experience into better future operations.

units.title: Closeout workflow
units.content: Confirm guest departure; execute safe strike; return rentals; reconcile vendor completion; secure media and documents; record incidents; compare budget; collect client feedback; run postmortem.

units.title: Closeout starts before the event
units.content: Return labels, asset owners, strike sequence, and deliverable deadlines should be planned before show day.

units.title: Closeout failures
units.content: Avoid leaving equipment ownership unclear, losing incident details, approving incomplete vendor work, and skipping review because the event is over.

drills.title: Run an event postmortem
drills.prompt: Create a closeout and lessons-learned record.
